description: List or search the company's own tracked shipments, newest first. Use it to find a shipment (free-text `q`: reference, customer reference, container number, vessel) or to filter by status (default active), carrier SCAC, phase, tag, ETA window (eta_after / eta_before, ISO 8601) or predicted eta_risk. For one shipment's full detail use get_shipment; for the next N days use list_arriving_shipments; for slipped ETAs use list_delayed_shipments; shipments other companies share with you are in list_shared_shipments. All arguments are optional. Returns: shipments[] {id, reference, ref_type, carrier, customer_reference, status, tracking_status, phase, pol, pod, eta, original_eta, delay_hours, predicted_eta, eta_risk, vessel, containers, booking_number, bl_number, tracked_via}, has_more, next_cursor. Paging: limit 1-100 (default 20); pass next_cursor as `cursor` for the next page.

company.description: Which company to act for: its id, @handle or exact name (see list_companies). Omit for the connection's default company.

eta_after.description: Only ETAs at or after this (ISO 8601).

eta_before.description: Only ETAs at or before this (ISO 8601).

eta_risk.description: Predicted ETA risk (estimate based on vessel position).

phase.description: Only shipments in this phase: pending (no carrier data yet), booked, in_transit, arrived or delivered.

q.description: Search text: reference, customer reference, container number or vessel name.

status.description: active (default) = being tracked; archived; or all.

tag.description: Only shipments with this tag (exact tag name, as shown in the web app).

name: list_shipments
title: List shipments
